title: Tesseract Analytics - POC scoping (latency SLOs & benchmarks)
summary: POC scoping call to align on latency and throughput SLOs for a 6-week POC. Customer wants clear TTFT and TPOT targets at p95/p99 for both interactive and batch scoring workloads; agreed on measurement plan, benchmark artifacts to run, and timeline for deliverables.
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark spreadsheet and sample config (Maya) by 2027-06-15
Tesseract to provide representative few-shot prompts and 1k sample requests (Samir) by 2027-06-18
action_items: Maya Chen: Share benchmark spreadsheet + prelim config (2027-06-15)
Ravi Patel: Prepare recommended cluster configs for interactive vs batch (2027-06-16)
Samir Desai: Provide 1k sample requests and input size distribution (2027-06-18)
Priya Kapoor: Confirm network topology and VPC peering constraints (2027-06-17)
Jordan Lee: Book follow-up review meeting (2027-06-18)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Maya from Redwood - AE on the account. Ravi's our SE, he'll lead the latency deep dive.
[00:08] Lena Morales: Hi, Lena here, CTO at Tesseract. We're focused on embedding gen + realtime summarization for our analytics product.
[00:12] Ravi Patel: great, glad to be here. quick agenda: agree success criteria, understand workload size, pick TTFT vs TPOT targets, and the measurement plan for the POC.
[00:22] Samir Desai: sounds good. our primary concern is latency for the interactive UI, but we also have nightly batch scoring that needs throughput.
[00:28] Priya Kapoor: and security constraints — VPC peering and KMS for keys. we'll need the private option if hosted network egress is an issue.
[01:05] Maya Chen: high level success criteria proposal: 1) interactive TTFT p95 under 250ms, TPOT p95 < 30ms/token for the core 1-2k token outputs; 2) batch throughput of X TPS on reserved capacity for 10M events per day. we can tune numbers after we see sample payloads.
[01:22] Lena Morales: when you say TTFT vs TPOT — can you define those quickly? sometimes our PMs mix them up.
[01:28] Ravi Patel: sure. TTFT is time to first token — so from request arrival to the first streaming token out. TPOT is time per output token — basically how quickly subsequent tokens are generated. both matter: TTFT for perceived latency, TPOT for long responses.
[01:40] Jordan Lee: so for a 200-token summary, TTFT affects the initial responsiveness and TPOT affects total completion time, right?
[01:45] Ravi Patel: exactly. and for UI we often optimize TTFT with faster kernels and lower context prep, and TPOT with batching/quantization choices.
[02:30] Samir Desai: our current baseline with OpenAI-ish endpoints is TTFT ~ 320ms p95 and TPOT ~ 45ms/token p95 for 1-2 token prompts. We're hoping Redwood can reduce that to target you mentioned.
[02:50] Maya Chen: good to know. we'll aim for that 250ms p95 and 30ms/token p95 as a starting SLA for the POC. For p99 we usually set a higher guardrail — maybe p99 TTFT 500ms and TPOT 70ms/token. Does that seem reasonable?
[03:06] Lena Morales: p99 500ms sounds okay as long as it's not frequent.
[03:12] Priya Kapoor: question on measurement: are you measuring from our client side or from the edge? network jitter will affect numbers.
[03:20] Ravi Patel: good point. measurement plan: two parallel measurements — synthetic server-side measurement (from Redwood's ingress) and client-side measurement from your app. We'll document both. for POC acceptance we'll use your in-app metrics to verify real user experience, but server-side numbers help triage.
[03:45] Jordan Lee: how do you handle cold starts and KV cache warm-up? our workloads include many unique sessions.
[03:52] Ravi Patel: we recommend a warm-up phase in the benchmark. Redwood runtime has KV cache and prefix caching. the measurement plan includes an initial warm-up set of 200 requests to populate caches, then steady-state runs. we'll also include a cold-start test.
[04:20] Samir Desai: workload sizing — our daily peak is about 300 RPS for interactive, but 95% are short prompts under 512 tokens; 5% are long summaries ~1.5k tokens. batch jobs run overnight at 150 RPS equivalent sustained for several hours.
[04:40] Maya Chen: perfect. we'll create two benchmark profiles: interactive (mixed short/long, bursty pattern) and batch (sustained throughput). We're going to simulate burst patterns with Poisson arrivals and also replay your sample traces.
[05:05] Priya Kapoor: we need to ensure any PII is masked — Samir will scrub samples. Also SSO and audit logs are required for compliance.
[05:12] Maya Chen: yes we will share SOC2 docs and audit log details.
[06:00] Ravi Patel: on target metrics, here's a proposed table (verbal): interactive TTFT targets: p50 60ms, p95 250ms, p99 500ms. TPOT: p50 12ms/token, p95 30ms/token, p99 70ms/token. For batch throughput targets we'll propose an end-to-end TPOT-equivalent throughput of ~2k tokens/sec on a small dedicated pool — we'll refine after we see token mix.
[06:25] Lena Morales: is quantization going to change quality? we've had regressions before.
[06:31] Ravi Patel: absolutely, quantization tradeoffs exist. Redwood Optimize will recommend quant profiles; in the POC we'll run quality regression tests using your eval prompts to ensure output fidelity stays within acceptable deltas. we'll capture perplexity and n-gram overlap plus human eval for a sample subset.
[07:05] Samir Desai: for benchmarks, what artifacts do you need from us?
[07:10] Maya Chen: best is: 1) sample request set (1k), 2) prompt templates and expected output lengths, 3) SLA priority list (what's most critical: TTFT vs throughput vs cost), and 4) any network constraints or region preferences.
[07:26] Samir Desai: we can provide that.
[08:00] Jordan Lee: timeline? you mentioned 6-week POC earlier.
[08:06] Maya Chen: recommended timeline: week 0 (prep): exchange artifacts and finalize bench config. Week 1: baseline hosted runs (no quant, default model) to capture current TTFT/TPOT. Week 2-3: tuning runs (kernel selection, quantization, batch policy) and dedicated reserved capacity tests. Week 4: run full regression evaluation and costs. Week 5: wrap-up and business review. total roughly 5-6 weeks.
[08:30] Priya Kapoor: do we need Dedicated for meaningful numbers or will hosted be enough?
[08:36] Ravi Patel: hosted baseline is fine to compare relative perf. Dedicated gives more predictable p99 behavior and higher sustained throughput; for batch throughput tests we'll spin up a Dedicated pool if you want production-like numbers. We can scope both.
[09:05] Samir Desai: curious about measurement tooling — are you providing a harness?
[09:10] Ravi Patel: yes, we'll provide a JMeter-like harness plus a lightweight client script that records TTFT, token-level timestamps, and includes warm-up phases. We'll also share a Google Sheet / benchmark spreadsheet with fields for config, run id, p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and TPOT, error rates, median tokens, cost estimate.
[09:40] Lena Morales: who will own the run? we have limited infra bandwidth.
[09:45] Maya Chen: Redwood can run the hosted baselines and send results; for private/dedicated tests we typically collaborate — your infra person (Priya) will help with VPC peering and any firewall rules, but Redwood SE will execute the runs.
[10:05] Priya Kapoor: noted. firewall rules will need to allow our CIDR to Redwood's test egress — I'll check internal policy.
[10:20] Samir Desai: about metrics — you mentioned token timestamps. are you able to stream per-token latency back so we can compute TPOT distribution?
[10:28] Ravi Patel: yes, the runtime logs per-token timing in the debug trace; the harness aggregates it. We'll provide both raw traces and processed percentiles. For privacy we can anonymize payloads.
[11:00] Jordan Lee: what about SLA acceptance criteria? how do we decide if POC succeeded?
[11:06] Maya Chen: propose success criteria: 1) interactive workload achieves TTFT p95 <= 250ms and TPOT p95 <= 30ms on your sample set in your app-measured client metrics; 2) batch throughput meets target within 15% of projected cost; 3) no regressions in quality beyond agreed threshold. If all three met, POC considered successful.
[11:30] Lena Morales: and if we miss one target?
[11:33] Maya Chen: we'll list risk buckets and remediation steps. we also include an optional extension window for two weeks to tune Dedicated configs.
[12:00] Samir Desai: small nit: our long prompt use-case is 1.5k output tokens. At TPOT 30ms/token that's still 45s which is long for UI. Could we stream partial summaries?
[12:12] Ravi Patel: yes, streaming partials is recommended. TTFT remains the critical metric. Also we can chunk outputs or use a structured output approach to surface interim results.
[12:50] Priya Kapoor: security again — KMS integration, HSM option?
[12:54] Maya Chen: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations; we'll send the compliance pack. For the POC we can do transcript redaction and tokens masked in logs.
[13:25] Jordan Lee: cost sensitivity — any rough cost delta between hosted and dedicated for these profiles?
[13:30] Ravi Patel: depends on model family and quantization. ballpark: dedicated can be 20-40% cheaper at scale due to reserved GPU amortization and better batching/sharing. We'll include cost modelling in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[14:05] Maya Chen: ok back to measurement plan specifics: we'll run these measurements and capture: client-side RTT to first byte, server ingress to first token, per-token timing, error rates, 95/99 latencies, and quality diffs. We'll also collect system metrics (GPU utilization, mem, kernel stalls) where possible.
[14:30] Samir Desai: will you include A/B tests between quant profiles?
[14:34] Ravi Patel: yes, we'll run multiple runs: baseline FP16, int8-ish quant, and a low-bit quant that trades quality. each run will have A/B comparisons against the eval set.
[15:00] Lena Morales: any recommended model family? we use open models but are flexible.
[15:06] Ravi Patel: for your use we'd start with a mid-sized open LLM that fits latency goals, something Redwood has curated in the catalog. if quality isn't adequate, we can move up. We'll provide model variants for the bench.
[16:00] Maya Chen: let's recap action items. Maya to send bench sheet and sample harness by 6/15; Ravi to propose cluster configs by 6/16; Samir to provide 1k requests by 6/18; Priya to confirm network constraints by 6/17; Jordan to schedule follow-up on 6/28.
[16:27] Jordan Lee: got it.
[16:33] Samir Desai: a couple more quick ops questions — tokenization differences across models and token accounting for cost.
[16:38] Ravi Patel: we'll normalize tokenization in the harness and show per-run token counts; cost estimates will use those normalized counts, with notes on model-specific differences.
[17:05] Lena Morales: last question — how do you handle p99 tail variability caused by noisy neighbors on shared hosted infra?
[17:12] Ravi Patel: that's exactly where Dedicated helps. on hosted we do multi-tenant smoothing, and we can route high-priority traffic to dedicated or priority lanes. Also we have fallback model variants to keep app online during spikes.
[18:00] Priya Kapoor: one operational ask — include a scripted checklist for our security review so we can turn this into a ticket internally.
[18:06] Maya Chen: we'll attach a security checklist and SOC2 docs in the follow-up email.
[18:40] Samir Desai: good. interesting if we could also see token-level heatmaps to debug long tail.
[18:46] Ravi Patel: yep we'll include heatmaps in the benchmark report.
[19:05] Jordan Lee: any blockers from Redwood side?
[19:09] Maya Chen: none; just waiting on your bench artifacts and Priya's network confirmation.
[19:20] Lena Morales: OK thanks everyone. we'll aim to get artifacts to you by next week.
[19:30] Maya Chen: thanks all. we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and schedule.
[20:00] [END RECORDING]

Notes about transcript quality: auto-generated, occasional name mislabels, some words transcribed phonetically (e.g., "kv cache" as "K V cash"), occasional run-on lines.

Benchmark plan (verbatim summary):
- Warm-up: 200 requests to prime caches.
- Interactive profile: 1k steady-state requests, mixed short/long ratio (95% <512 tokens, 5% >1k tokens), burst tests at 300 RPS for 2 minutes.
- Batch profile: sustained replay of 10k requests across several hours; dedicated pool test for throughput.
- Metrics: TTFT (client and server), TPOT (p50/p95/p99), error rates, GPU util, token counts, quality diffs.
- Acceptance: interactive TTFT p95 <= 250ms and TPOT p95 <= 30ms measured from client; p99 guardrails as discussed.

References shared on call: "benchmark spreadsheet link (placeholder)", "SOC2 package (link)", "Redwood private deployment notes (link)".
